To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
quizzing improves learning of material from a sixth grade social studies course and that this effect is robust across different types of assessments.
In the classroom, students' performance on tests improved following low-stakes quizzes, even when the tests were not identical to the quizzes.
quizzing promotes students' long-term learning and retention of social studies course material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of quizzing in a classroom setting.
the effects of quizzing on learning in a social studies course in the classroom.
the question of whether students can learn better in the classroom by being quizzed on course material, and we find evidence that the answer is "yes".
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quizzing students on course material is a useful learning strategy for students in the classroom.
retrieval practice in classroom setting is a powerful learning tool.
quizzing is effective in promoting long-term learning and retention of the material in a social studies course.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students should quiz themselves more often, both in the classroom and out of class.
retrieval practice is an effective learning strategy that is easy to implement in the classroom and that has the potential to increase student learning and retention of academic content.
students should be quizzed on material they need to learn, and the more they are quizzed, the better they will perform on exams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers can easily incorporate quizzing in their classroom and students should be encouraged to quiz themselves as well.
teachers should be encouraged to use low-stakes testing as an integral part of their instruction.
quizzing is not only an effective way to assess students' learning, but it also improves their long-term retention of the material.
